mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy is affected.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% over three months signals strong consumer demand, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it indicates a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs increase.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is rising, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic contraction reduces corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and UNRATE rising
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.
